# Gayle Fallon — scholarly videogame reference

- Original title: A Review of Robin Hood Scholarship Published in 2016
- Source: [Original publication](https://openjournals.bsu.edu/biarhs/article/download/3009/1759)
- Author / publisher: Gayle Fallon; Bulletin of the International Association for Robin Hood Studies, volume 2
- Language / date: English; 2018
- Access: PDF text inspected, particularly PDF page five, printed page 25.
- Checked: 2026-09-09

Fallon’s scholarship review identifies Thomas Rowland’s chapter, “And Now Begins Our Game: Revitalizing the Ludic Robin Hood,” as a study of Robin Hood videogames and their relationship to earlier play traditions. Spellbound’s 2002 game is one of three titles singled out for particular attention.

The [publisher’s contents listing](https://www.routledge.com/Robin-Hood-in-Outlawed-Spaces-Media-Performance-and-Other-New-Directions/Coote-Johnson/p/book/9781032097459) independently identifies Rowland’s contribution as chapter eleven of Robin Hood in Outlaw/ed Spaces. The chapter itself was not retrieved; this record summarizes Fallon’s account, not an inspection of Rowland’s full argument.
